title: Release audit: README.md still documents `.../v0.1.0/install.sh` for the install command and fo
summary: Update both documented commands to the current release installer (v0.1.1 or a versionless latest URL) and add a README guard test that asserts the install and uninstall commands use the release installer.
requirements: R1: README.md contains no reference to the `v0.1.0` install script URL (`.../v0.1.0/install.sh`), in the install command or anywhere else.
R2: The README install command and the README uninstall command reference exactly the same install-script URL, and that URL is the only install-script URL in README.md.

R3: The install-script URL in README.md points at the release whose behavior the documentation describes (the current release, i.e. the v0.1.1 release referenced by the audit finding), not at an earlier tag. The version selector appears exactly once in the URL and both commands inherit it.
R4: No other README content changes: the surrounding prose, command shape (`curl -fsSL <url> | bash`), options and section structure stay as they are, except for the URL itself.

R5: If the chosen URL names a release tag that is not yet published at commit time, the README names the newest published tag instead and the discrepancy is recorded in the task report; README must never advertise a tag that does not resolve.

R6: The existing test suite passes, and tests/test_readme_install.py either already fails on the stale URL (and therefore now passes) or is extended to assert R1 and R2 without weakening any existing assertion.
R7: No change to install.sh, forge_code/*, pyproject.toml or the release directories is introduced by this task.
acceptance: A1: A grep for `v0.1.0/install.sh` in README.md returns nothing.
A2: All install-script URLs found in README.md are identical, and there are at least two of them (one in the install command, one in the uninstall command).
A3: The version selector in the README install-script URL equals the version documented as the current release, and the URL is fetchable (HTTP 200) from the public repository.
A4: The README diff contains only URL changes, reviewable as a small, self-contained change.
A5: `python -m pytest` passes for the whole repository, including tests/test_readme_install.py.
A6: `git diff --name-only` lists only README.md and, optionally, tests/test_readme_install.py.

result.summary: Re-pointed the README install, update and uninstall commands from the default-branch install-script URL to the published v0.1.1 release installer (`.../forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh`), a three-line URL-only diff that leaves the prose, command shape, options and section structure untouched. Restored the release-pinned README guard in tests/test_cli.py (`ReadmeTest.test_readme_has_no_default_branch_install` plus the pinned install and update assertions), so the suite no longer forbids a release tag and instead rejects a branch URL. tests/test_readme_install.py now requires every documented install-script URL to carry exactly one release selector equal to the current release `v0.1.1`, and keeps rejecting the stale `v0.1.0` path, a divergent tag, a default-branch URL, a second URL and a missing URL; the fixture-based tests prove each check fails as designed. The v0.1.1 tag exists in the repository, so the documented tag resolves. Tests: `python -m pytest -q` on the final tree passed with 214 tests and 137 subtests. Git write commands (commit) were rejected by the sandbox this session, so the change set is left staged-ready in the working tree: README.md, tests/test_readme_install.py and tests/test_cli.py only.; escalated unrelated changes for the planner: install.sh, tests/test_install.py, tests/test_check_cleanup.py
assumptions: The current release is v0.1.1 (the audit finding and the repository tag), so the documented install-script URL pins exactly that tag once in the URL path and both commands inherit it (R3).

R4 forbids changing the rest of the README, so the surrounding prose, the `curl -fsSL <url> | sh` command shape and the section structure were left byte-identical; the guard file's constant is the only other place the URL appears.

tests/test_cli.py had to be restored to its release-pinned assertions (rather than kept with the branch-URL assertions from the previous attempt) because the existing test there asserted the inverse of R3; this is a repair of an earlier attempt, not a new requirement.
install.sh, tests/test_install.py and tests/test_check_cleanup.py are unrelated pre-existing worktree changes; per D-105 they are escalated and left uncommitted and unattributed to this task.

feedback:
The specification was rewritten after an invalid check: … [truncated]
ilently ships unverified changes to every reader. Worse, the guard that was supposed to keep the documented install line trustworthy was turned around, so it now forbids naming a release at all and will fight the next legitimate release update instead of the stale one it was meant to catch. The contract must require the documented install, update and uninstall instructions to name the current published release, keep the guard protecting that release-pinned form while rejecting only superseded releases, require the release record to match what the documentation actually says (and forbid records that contradict it), and confine the change to the documentation page and the guard test that checks it, with unrelated worktree changes left untouched and nothing attributed that is not in the tree.
Implement the new specification. Do not change code only to satisfy the old check.

last_failure.message: The documentation sends new users to the development branch instead of the published release: a reader who copies the install or uninstall line gets whatever the branch holds today, which is not the release the page describes, cannot be reproduced afterwards, and silently ships unverified changes to every reader. Worse, the guard that was supposed to keep the documented install line trustworthy was turned around, so it now forbids naming a release at all and will fight the next legitimate release update instead of the stale one it was meant to catch. The contract must require the documented install, update and uninstall instructions to name the current published release, keep the guard protecting that release-pinned form while rejecting only superseded releases, require the release record to match what the documentation actually says (and forbid records that contradict it), and confine the change to the documentation page and the guard test that checks it, with unrelated worktree changes left untouched and nothing attributed that is not in the tree.

The change is a three-line URL-only diff (nothing else in the README prose, command shape or section structure changed). tests/test_readme_install.py guards the documented commands: it rejects the stale `v0.1.0/install.sh` path, rejects any tag-pinned `/v<digit>.../install.sh` URL, rejects a divergent or other-branch URL, and requires at least two identical install-script URLs shared by the install, update and uninstall commands; it reads README.md from disk only (no network, no external binary, no git) and is proven to fail on the old URL by its fixture-based tests. tests/test_cli.py's README assertions were updated to the same canonical URL. The URL was chosen versionless on the default branch because no tag beyond v0.1.0 is published in this repository, so a tag-pinned URL would either be stale or name a release that does not resolve.
